opportunities.name: Power settlement reconciliation: congestion revenue, PMAs and counterparty disputes
opportunities.description: The Portland real-time desk hand-calculates CAISO congestion relief revenue and emails it to the flash and settlement group to check against the next morning's flash. Volume Management recalculates it by hour. At month-end, desk heads and support review prior-month adjustments line by line and query mismatches with Settlements. They also reconcile ISO revenue against volume management and work counterparty disputes (El Paso Electric, SRP, MPC), which means requesting trade tapes and reconstructing what happened on specific hours.
opportunities.stall_points: Amounts are hand-calculated, and hours go missing from both sides' calculations and from the CAISO site. One-sided PMAs, such as revenue reversed with no cost reversed, stay open across several emails. Disputes drag for months, and tape access goes through another person. About 30 disputes arose from EOL deals altered without notes. Sheets go to the wrong recipients.
opportunities.automation: Compute hourly congestion revenue from CAISO award files and schedules, and reconcile it automatically against the flash, the inc sheet and settlement entries, alerting only on mismatches. PMA lines would be matched to Enpower deal changes so one-sided adjustments are flagged, and a dispute tracker would link each disputed deal to its tape, evidence and decision, with a required reason field on deal alterations.
opportunities.estimate_rationale: Observer estimates run from 15 minutes for flash notes to 90 minutes for month-end PMA and ISO true-ups, with a median of 45 minutes. Calculation and matching automate well, but dispute resolution does not, so the fraction is set at the 0.4 median.

opportunities.name: Meter flow without a valid deal: extension, new-deal and write-off requests
opportunities.description: Volume management, logistics and settlement staff find gas flowing at an HPL meter with no active Sitara deal. The deal may have expired or missed its evergreen roll, the flow may be parked on the Strangers Gas contract, or the meter may be new. They email Daren Farmer, one meter at a time, asking him to extend or roll a deal, create a new one, or sign a printed write-off to Unaccounted for Gas. Allocation, accounting arrangements and invoicing cannot go ahead until he answers. This is the largest and most frequent process in the archive. Nearly every batch shows it, and almost all of it runs through one person.
opportunities.stall_points: Every request waits on Daren Farmer, who is also trading, so requesters send reminders and the same meters come back the next month. Write-offs need a printed, signed and returned original. Forwarded threads carry long quoted history. Feedback and bridge errors pass through four or five people before reaching the deal owner. Deal numbers are sometimes wrong or sit with another desk, and suspended counterparties or expired contracts block the fix.
opportunities.automation: A daily and month-end exception job that compares allocated meter flow with active Sitara deals and lists every meter with flow and no deal, including Strangers Gas allocations and lapsed evergreens. Each exception goes to the deal owner as a pre-filled work item with the meter, days, volume and the prior deal proposed for extension, plus one-click options to extend, create or approve a write-off electronically, with status tracking and automatic reminders. This replaces the one-off emails, the printed approval forms and the chasers.
opportunities.estimate_rationale: Observers' estimates ranged from 15 to 90 minutes. Most clustered at 15 to 25 minutes across requester and approver, so the median of 20 minutes is used. Detection and routing automate well, but the commercial decision to extend, re-deal or write off stays human, so the fraction is held at the median of 0.5.

opportunities.name: Real-time power schedule, cut and variance corrections
opportunities.description: Real-time shift traders spend part of each day correcting schedules and positions. When Colstrip or a counterparty cuts, they zero deals and book offsetting annuities. They fix import IDs and load zones, create DA and HA finals in CAPS, and run the SAR and INC reconciliation against CAPS and Enpower. They also repair El Paso Electric schedules with missing tags, check out schedules with counterparties by phone, and call generators every hour for checkout. The same cut is recorded in several places, including paper cut sheets and a Lotus Notes database, and procedures are re-issued when entries are inconsistent.
opportunities.stall_points: Variances are found after the fact and need detective work. Real-time cuts are not in CAPS, so the SAR and INC only match after manual additions. HA finals creation hits SQL errors and data scrape failures that go unnoticed over weekends. The EPE schedule sheet misses tags day after day. Paper cut sheets get lost, and hourly generator calls are sometimes missed.
opportunities.automation: A cut-entry form that zeroes the deal, books the offsetting annuity and logs the cut once to every destination. An automated morning SAR, INC and CARP comparison would write the reconciliation sheet. Tags in the EPE schedule would be validated automatically against dispatcher schedules, and the scrape and finals imports would be monitored with alerts. Metered generator output would be pulled into the services sheet automatically.
opportunities.estimate_rationale: Observer estimates cluster at 20 to 45 minutes with a median of 30 minutes per occurrence. Detection and logging are automatable, but resupply and counterparty checkout decisions stay human, so the fraction is set at the 0.45 median.

opportunities.description: On the Portland real-time desk, Bill Williams, prescheduling and the cash desks email the shift whenever the book is short or long. opportunities.name: Gas volume, imbalance and pathing reconciliation
opportunities.description: Volume management, logistics and settlement analysts reconcile gas volumes across MOPS, POPS, Sitara, Unify and pipeline statements. They work allocation exceptions, UA4 and zero-volume feed problems, measurement and nomination-versus-flow gaps, production imbalances and intercompany or interdesk variances, and they clear unpathed deals and bridge-back errors before the month-end close cutoff. Transwestern does the equivalent reconciliation with El Paso and other pipelines. Each item is researched by hand and then chased by email to whoever must re-path, reallocate or correct the volume.
opportunities.stall_points: Fixes need the right person to act in POPS or Unify, and ownership of pipelines and paths is often unclear after reassignments. The same variances come back for weeks. Zero-volume feeds are overridden by hand each night because the system team has not fixed the root cause. Pipeline meter statements arrive by fax on request. Bridge-back errors must be cleared against a hard clock time, and multi-step tasks such as meter replacements wait on each hand-off.
opportunities.automation: A daily reconciliation job that compares nominated, confirmed, measured and allocated volumes across MOPS, POPS, Sitara, Unify and loaded pipeline statements. It flags zero-feed meters, one-sided intercompany deals, unpathed deals and bridge-back errors, and puts each exception in a shared queue with an owner from a pipeline and zone registry, an age, and automatic reminders ahead of the close cutoff. This replaces manual spreadsheet research and forwarded issue lists.
opportunities.estimate_rationale: Observers estimated 20 to 120 minutes because items need multi-party research, and the median is 45 minutes. Detection and routing automate well, but root-cause research and counterparty agreement do not, so the fraction is set at the median of about 0.35.

opportunities.name: Risk book administration: book setup, deal rebooks, book flips and price corrections
opportunities.description: Darron Giron and the risk book administrators receive a steady flow of requests. Some ask for new trading books, portfolios, curves and mappings in TAGG, Sitara, CPR, TDS and Global Counterparty. Others ask to flip deals between books (for example ECC and Canadian deals to FT-US/CAND-ERMS), rebook counterparties, change deal rates or demand charges, add missing Sitara, TAGG or EOL cross-references, and supply book lists or reference ids. opportunities.stall_points: Requests go to several different administrators, and routing is unclear (for example, a TAGG book must first exist in Global Counterparty). Requests arrive piecemeal and urgently for same-day invoicing. Cross-system ids are not linked, so lookups are manual. Recurring monthly rate changes sit unactioned until chased. Book lists are rebuilt for each requester.
opportunities.automation: One intake form and queue for book, curve and mapping setup that routes to every system's administrator and shows status. A bulk deal-attribute change tool would take a list of deal numbers with the target book or counterparty. A rule would flag deals with Canadian counterparties in US books, and recurring rate changes would load from the monthly price source. Validation at entry would auto-link TAGG, Sitara and EOL ids, and a maintained book and portfolio reference table would serve book lists.
opportunities.estimate_rationale: Observer estimates centre on 15 to 30 minutes with a median of 20 minutes. Most changes are mechanical once approved, so the fraction is set at the 0.5 median.

opportunities.name: Month-end P&L close, valuation and audit support requests
opportunities.description: At month-end and quarter-end the risk desks close the books: last-day files, economics and OA reviews, P&L restatements and write-off decisions. They also field repeated requests for support. Arthur Andersen asks for P&L top pages and curve shift reports, risk asks for curve validation explanations, accounting asks for liquidation support, and the Confirmations group asks for back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audits. Darron Giron receives most requests and forwards them to analysts, who rebuild the support by hand each month.
opportunities.stall_points: Requests arrive as second requests and are forwarded several times. Owners are out and requests go unseen. There is no system with back-dated curves, so a risk person is interrupted for each valuation. Gas accounting cannot start until every desk replies, and errors such as killed January activity are found after close, forcing restatements.
opportunities.automation: A month-end checklist that tracks desk completion with variance checks on the P&L tabs. Standard extracts for top pages, curve shifts and liquidation support per region would be filed automatically to the shared directory, and a valuation tool with back-dated curves would let Confirmations self-serve MTM. An auditor request tracker would map each desk to its preparer.
opportunities.estimate_rationale: Observer estimates run from 20 to 120 minutes with a median of 45 minutes. Extract generation helps, but much of the work is analysis and explanation, so the fraction is set at the 0.3 median.

opportunities.name: Gas invoice and deal price discrepancy resolution
opportunities.description: Settlements and accounting staff compare counterparty invoices, statements and payment claims with Sitara and Unify. They find price differences, missing days, wrong counterparties or one-sided deals, then email the deal owner (Daren Farmer, Julie Meyers) to confirm the right deal and price and to correct the ticket so Unify can be redrafted. The owner often has to ask a trader or the counterparty before answering. Invoice deadlines and counterparty phone calls keep up the pressure while questions bounce between people.
opportunities.stall_points: Requests sit with one or two deal owners and are re-sent when they are out. Questions bounce between settlements, logistics, measurement and traders for days or weeks, and invoice and payment cut-offs pass. Some disputes run for months, and counterparties call repeatedly. Volume Management sometimes shows no actualized volume, so nobody can confirm the amount.
opportunities.automation: An automatic invoice-to-deal match that compares each counterparty invoice or statement line with the Sitara deal price, volume, counterparty and entity. Each mismatch is raised as a tracked case routed to the ticket owner, carrying the deal, the invoice line and the allocation already attached. Corrections in Sitara notify settlements automatically so Unify can be redrafted, which replaces the email threads and chasers.
opportunities.estimate_rationale: Observer medians cluster at 25 to 45 minutes, and the message-weighted median is 30 minutes across requester and owner. Matching and routing automate well, but resolving the true price with traders or counterparties does not, so the fraction is set at the 0.4 median.

opportunities.name: Manager surveys, budget, HR and administrative data collection
opportunities.description: Finance, cost-model, HR and admin groups email managers each month or cycle asking them to complete hours and activity-driver surveys, cost-center allocation percentages, budget and staffing worksheets, variance explanations, presentation inputs and weekly bullets. Other requests cover PEP and PRC reviewer lists and feedback, analyst recruiting forms, onboarding items, time reports, expense approvals and phone-bill reviews. opportunities.stall_points: Few people respond by the deadline, so reminders and new deadlines follow. The same driver numbers are re-keyed every month. Protected or distorted spreadsheets bounce back to finance. HR systems such as PEP were down or had wrong reporting lines, so lists went by email through intermediaries. HR asks for the same placement fields more than once, and each expense report is a separate click-through.
opportunities.automation: One collection workflow with forms pre-filled from the prior period and from system reports (driver counts, allocations, reporting lines). It would validate totals, send automatic reminders only to non-responders, and track status for the requester. Expense approvals would be delegated or rule-based, with a digest for exceptions. This replaces the broadcast emails, attachments and chasers.
opportunities.estimate_rationale: Observer estimates span 4 to 60 minutes, and the median across the merged items is 30 minutes per manager cycle. Prefill and reminders automate a good share, but the content still needs owner judgement, so the fraction is set at the 0.4 median.

opportunities.name: Customer and producer gas nomination intake and re-keying
opportunities.description: Customers, producers and pipelines send daily, weekend and monthly gas nominations and revisions by email. Examples include Calpine, Enron Methanol and MTBE, KCS Josey Ranch, TXU, Reliant, Valero and Prize Energy, and the nominations usually come as Word or spreadsheet attachments with little body text. Ami Chokshi and other trade-support staff forward them to schedulers. Schedulers re-key the volumes into Sitara, POPS or Unify and ask Daren Farmer to approve revisions, and risk prepares next-month estimates from prior-month noms. Each revision repeats the cycle, so the same customer can generate several rounds a month.
opportunities.stall_points: Attachments arrive with blank subjects and no body text and are forwarded by hand. Each file has to be opened and re-keyed, and entry mistakes creep in. Revisions need Daren's approval before anything changes. Nominations sometimes arrive before the transport contract or meter number exists, and unresponsive producers have to be chased against deadlines. Estimates are sent in fragments.
opportunities.automation: A nomination ingestion service that reads the nomination emails and attachments into structured rows (counterparty, meter, day, volume). It diffs each row against the current Sitara and POPS volumes, posts only the changes to the scheduling queue for one-click approval, and auto-acknowledges the sender when nothing changed. It also proposes next-month estimates and swing volumes from prior-month and prior-year flow. This replaces the manual forwarding, re-keying and approval emails.
opportunities.estimate_rationale: Observer estimates ran from 10 to 30 minutes, with a median of 15 minutes per nomination or revision including forwarding, keying and approval. Parsing and diffing structured attachments is highly automatable, but judgement on swings and revisions remains, so the fraction is set at the 0.5 median.

opportunities.name: Gas pipeline outage, cut and on-call notice relay
opportunities.description: Gas control, field staff, plant contacts and schedulers email long distribution lists about pipeline maintenance, meter shut-ins, plant upsets, capacity reductions and pipeline cuts. Weekend on-call staff also send narrative notes. Schedulers read each notice, work out which nominations are affected, and decide whether to zero volumes, buy back, cut, or negotiate with the producer. Updates come as repeated forwards that revise earlier notices.
opportunities.stall_points: Notices are typed by hand and sent to 15 to 40 people. Each reschedule is a new forwarded chain that has to be re-read. The volume decision waits on someone mapping the notice to nominations, and producer notice letters are written by hand. On-call notes are free text or attachments with no body, and cuts are relayed after the fact.
opportunities.automation: A shared outage and cut log keyed by meter and pipeline, populated from gas control and pipeline notices. It matches each event against open nominations, alerts the owning scheduler with a proposed volume change, auto-generates producer notice letters, and publishes a structured weekend on-call summary. This replaces the free-text broadcast emails and re-forwards.
opportunities.estimate_rationale: Observer estimates range from 10 to 30 minutes per notice across sender and readers, with a median of 20 minutes. Matching and distribution automate well, but the nomination decision remains a judgement call, so the fraction is set at the 0.4 median.

opportunities.name: Transport contract, amendment and OBA administration
opportunities.description: Shippers email Transwestern's account director (Michelle Lokay) to raise contract quantity for a day or two, change receipt points, continue capacity or amend OBAs. She approves each request and forwards it to contract administration (Dennis Lee, Craig Buehler), who generate the amendment. opportunities.stall_points: One-day changes mean the same contract is re-requested, re-approved and re-forwarded several times. Customer revisions arrive after the original request. Contracts wait on missing CAFs, credit approval or legal. Status is compiled into emails by hand, and the sharing calculation for capacity-release billing is redone each month.
opportunities.automation: A request-to-amendment workflow that captures contract, quantity, dates, points and rate in structured fields. It would route for approval and credit check and push the change to the contract system with status visible to all parties. It would also query active deals by contract before termination, generate the contract status and termination report on a schedule, and encode capacity-release sharing rules in billing.
opportunities.estimate_rationale: Observer estimates range from 10 minutes for a simple approval to 60 minutes for billing adjustments and reports, with a median of 25 minutes. Intake and routing automate well, and approvals stay human, so the fraction is set at 0.45.

opportunities.name: Standing procedure reminders and market notice broadcasts
opportunities.description: Desk managers broadcast standing rules and market changes to their groups by email. On the real-time power desk these cover CAISO and FERC notices, price caps, path derates, tagging, congestion bidding, time zones and delivery points. opportunities.stall_points: Each notice is forwarded separately to several people, sometimes weeks late or without its attachment. opportunities.automation: Auto-route CAISO and market notices to the desk distribution list with a summary and an acknowledgement tracker. Keep the desk rules on one maintained page, and encode the key rules as validation at deal entry: lock EOL-sourced tickets, check tier bids, time zones and delivery points, and require the physical flag. This replaces repeated broadcast reminders.
opportunities.estimate_rationale: Observer estimates range from 3 to 25 minutes with a median of 10 minutes per notice including reading and correcting. Routing is fully automatable, but interpretation is not, so the fraction is set at about the 0.45 median.
